title: Validate fares and timestamps
prompt: Some trips in the export can't be right: a dropoff before the pickup, a trip that went nowhere, a fare that was reversed. Write `trip_metrics(trips)`. It starts from your `trip_times(trips)`, keeps only the trips that pass every check below, and gives each one its length in minutes.
rules: `trip_seconds` is more than 0: the dropoff comes after the pickup. A missing time fails.
`trip_distance` is more than 0. A missing distance fails.
`fare` is more than 0. A missing, zero or negative fare fails, even when `total` is positive.
A zone id that isn't in the zone list doesn't fail a trip: the next step deals with zones.

Return `trip_id`, `pickup_utc`, `pickup_date`, `pickup_hour`, `pickup_zone_id`, `dropoff_zone_id`, `trip_distance`, `trip_minutes`, `fare` and `total`, in that order. `trip_minutes` is `trip_seconds` ÷ 60 as a `DECIMAL(8,2)`.
hints: Call `trip_times(trips)` first, so `trip_seconds` is already there.
Three conditions joined with `&`, each in parentheses. A comparison with a missing value is never true, so missing values fail on their own.
`(F.col("trip_seconds") / 60).cast("decimal(8,2)")` gives minutes, rounded half up to two decimals.
explanation: Every check is a strict `>`. A trip of zero seconds or zero miles is a meter that was started and stopped, not a ride, and a zero fare isn't a sale. Checking `fare` rather than `total` matters: a no-charge trip with a 0.50 surcharge has a positive total but earned nothing. A comparison with `NULL` is never true, so a trip with a missing time, distance or fare drops out without a separate `isNotNull`. Minutes are kept as an exact `DECIMAL`, so the averages built on them later come out the same on every run.
